sources.citation: Romadhan, Achmad Dicky, Muhammad Thobroni, Alien Kurnia Warya Selia & Nurul Hanna Fauziyyah. 2026. Perilaku Sintaksis Predikat Verba Bahasa Dayak Agabag. EDU-KATA: Jurnal Bahasa, Sastra dan Pembelajarannya 12(1): 42-52. Lamongan: Universitas Islam Darul Ulum. (CC BY-SA)

sources.citation: Ayu Putri Dahlia. 2023. Bentuk dan Makna Kata Ulang Bahasa Dayak Tenggalan di Desa Mansalong Kabupaten Nunukan Provinsi Kalimantan Utara (Kajian Morfologi). sources.note: no phonology content: reduplication morphology only (35 reduplicated forms from Mansalong classified by base and meaning: full, partial, affixed, 'perubahan fonem' types); chapter II.H gives location/affiliation of Dayak Tenggalan; no sound-system section, no transcription notes, zero occurrences of tekanan/aksen/intonasi/prosodi/suku kata stress remarks; forms cited in plain orthography without stress marks.

sources.note: Only modern linguist-collected data on Murut Sembakung and Tingalan (800-item wordlists + functors); the introduction's transcription notes are the most likely place for a first-hand remark on accent/vowel length in these varieties.

sources.citation: Hartatik. 2014. Perbandingan bahasa dan data arkeologi pada suku Tidung dan Dayak di wilayah Nunukan: data bantu untuk rekonstruksi sejarah dan perubahan budaya. Naditira Widya 8(1): 29-48. Banjarbaru: Balai Arkeologi Banjarmasin. doi:10.24832/nw.v8i1.104
sources.note: no phonology content: comparative vocabulary tables (Indonesian / Agabag / Tahol / Tenggalan / Tidung, 12 semantic groups, pp. 32-38) with similarity percentages (Tabel 2), then archaeological objects and oral traditions; p. 31 states the comparison is lexical only and 'belum secara khusus mengarah pada sistem bunyi (fonetik) dan susunan bunyi (fonologis)' (does not yet specifically address the sound system); forms in plain orthography without stress marks; zero occurrences of tekanan/aksen/intonasi/prosodi/nada.

sources.note: Nothing for Murut Sembakung/Tingalan: they appear only in subgrouping lists and functor tables; the only stress remarks in the dissertation concern Philippine languages (and a general footnote that most languages of Mindanao 'and areas further south have lost contrastive stress', p. 287 n.3, not specific to this language).
